documentation.rationale: The identity/terms half is present: VIN, out-the-door price including all dealer fees, and a history summary flagging accident and multiple owners. The maintenance half is absent: no service records, no accident repair details, no underside or engine-bay photos.

condition.rationale: An accident/damage event is reported with no repair documentation. The front bumper shows a visible notch/split by the driver-side grille, and the cluster photo shows a lit TPMS lamp. The interior looks tidy and the tires are matching Michelins, but date codes, underside and mechanicals are not shown.

price_value.rationale: The $21,784 asking price is above the fair-value range of $17,333-$20,790 (mid $18,676), despite a reported accident that should discount it. Peers include a 2017 at 41k for $21,075 and a 2017 base at 57k for $18,500.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual, naturally aspirated, reliable, simple, and inside the ceiling, so it fits a point-of-view bridge. The reported accident and price premium weaken the 6-24 month resale case.

logistics.rationale: California dealer about 326 mi away, so CA registration and smog are straightforward. Third-party PPI access is not stated.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: 860 Special Edition in Halo with the 6-speed manual, Torsen LSD and orange-stitched interior: one genuinely desirable special-edition trait on a car that appears stock.

evidence.mission_note: A stock-appearing 860 SE manual with a simple naturally aspirated drivetrain fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and sits inside the price ceiling. The reported accident directly affects the easy-resale part of the mission until it is documented.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly to a 2017 Toyota 86 coupe, the photos show a 6-speed manual and factory 860 SE trim in Halo, and the price is stated as including all dealer fees. Against that, the dealer's own history summary reports an accident/damage event with multiple owners and supplies no detail or repair invoices. The front photo shows a notch/split in the bumper beside the driver-side grille opening. The cluster photo reads 44,487 mi against the listed 44,215, a minor gap, and shows an amber TPMS lamp of unclear status. No service records, tire date codes, underside photos, tune status or track-use disclosure are provided, so all three model-critical concerns that apply remain open. The asking price of $21,784 sits above the mileage-adjusted fair range of $17,333-$20,790 despite the reported accident.
evidence.next_action: Ask California Motor Trade for the full history report with accident details and any repair invoice, and confirm in writing that a third-party PPI near Norco is allowed before any deposit.
